events.content:
Partial prerendering is enabled and verified. ## What changed `next.config.ts` — one line: ```ts const nextConfig: NextConfig = { cacheComponents: true, } ``` The important detail: this project is on Next.js **16.4.0-canary.8**, and the old `experimental.ppr` flag is a *hard error* there: ``` `experimental.ppr` has been merged into `cacheComponents`. The Partial Prerendering feature is still available, but is now enabled via `cacheComponents`. ``` There's also no longer a per-route `export const experimental_ppr = true` opt-in — `cacheComponents` is a top-level (no longer experimental) flag that applies app-wide. `tsconfig.json` picked up `.next/dev/types/**/*.ts` in `include`, which the build adds automatically. I reverted the array reformatting it also did, so the diff stays to the one real line. ## Verification The build reports `- Cache Components enabled` and the route table now marks `/` as partially prerendered: ``` ┌ ◐ / ◐ (Partial Prerender) prerendered as static HTML with dynamic server-streamed content ``` The prerendered shell in `.next/server/app/index.html` confirms the split is where you'd want it: ```html

Store

Loading products...

Loading recommendations...

``` The static shell (`
`, the heading, both fallbacks) is baked at build time; the two `` markers are the dynamic holes streamed in per request. No code changes were needed in `app/` — the existing `` boundaries in `page.tsx` were already the right shape, and they're what makes this work: the build didn't fail on the unreachable `api.example.com` fetches because the prerender aborts cleanly at each boundary. ## One thing worth deciding Right now *both* sections are dynamic, so the prerendered part is just the page chrome. If the product list doesn't need to be per-request fresh, adding `"use cache"` to `getProducts` in `app/ProductList.tsx` would pull the rendered list into the static shell and leave only `Recommendations` as a dynamic hole — a much bigger PPR win. I didn't do that unprompted since it changes data-freshness semantics for pricing, which is your call. Say the word and I'll wire it up, optionally with a `cacheLife` profile to bound staleness.

shellCommands.command: git log --oneline -5 && git status --short && git diff
find /workspace/app /workspace/__agent_eval__ -type f | head -50 && echo "--- next.config ---" && cat /workspace/next.config.ts && echo "--- tsconfig ---" && cat /workspace/tsconfig.json
ls .next/server/app/ && echo "=== SHELL HTML ===" && cat .next/server/app/index.html 2>/dev/null | head -c 1500
git diff --stat && echo "=== tsconfig diff ===" && git diff tsconfig.json
npx next build 2>&1 | tail -12 && echo "=== final diff ===" && git diff -- next.config.ts tsconfig.json
